Reframing the statement through the lens of the Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report (FSR) tempers the initially “mildly positive” read. The FSR highlights elevated vulnerabilities in business debt (notably leveraged loans and weaker underwriting), pockets of stretched asset valuations, and fragilities in short-term funding markets—evidenced around this period by repo market strains—while noting that banks’ capital and liquidity are strong and household leverage is moderate. These stability considerations amplify the downside risks flagged by the FOMC (soft business investment, weaker external demand) and help explain the Committee’s data-dependent easing and continued reinvestments/implementation steps to maintain smooth market functioning. Taken together, the outlook remains supported by a strong labor market and resilient core financial intermediaries, but the FSR’s vulnerability map warrants a more cautious tilt than a purely macro read would suggest.

Bottom line: supportive but more guarded than before, given corporate leverage and funding-market fragilities offset by bank resilience and policy support.
